notes: The prompt declares a creature-collecting adventure RPG, so both genres are named with RPG leading, since the party, turn-based battles, crafting and equipment progression are the loop while exploration is how it is delivered; the Turn-based RPG preset is modelled on exactly this kind of creature-collecting game. Shape is world-open, which RPG words as a single contiguous map with town, roads and clearings on one surface, because the author chose to keep the dungeon a cave on the same map rather than an instance — that answer also settles the route: entering the cave from the wilderness is a real outside-to-inside transition, so P3 is required by a feature plainly present rather than assumed, where the instanced alternative they rejected would have been P4. The wilderness is hilly enough to hold a cave mouth, so terrain-relief comes in at its tiered cost, and I read the cave interior as a separately generated interior rather than an overhanging tunnel in the surface frame, which is what keeps this off P2. Decided without a user: I dropped the preset's gate-progression because nothing here gates ground by level, left building-interior out so only the cave is entered and village shops stay street-side, used collectible-nodes for both crafting materials and the creature eggs found in the wilderness, and let landmark-focal carry the meaningful points of interest the author wanted along a two-to-three minute crossing; the worn exploration trail is Adventure's row rather than one RPG offers, and riding, hatching, party management and save/load are mechanics with no layout expression.
